INTRODUCTION

The (Selespeed) electro-hydraulic transmission system is designed to improve the performance of the manual mechanical transmission components.

The system means that the driver does not have to control the clutch pedal and the gear lever affording them the pleasure of driving that comes from the direct control of the transmission.

It also improves driving safety through a direct control of driver errors.

The system basically consists of a manual transmission, with a dry, single plate clutch and manual gearbox with synchromesh with hydraulic power assistance.

Neither the clutch nor the gearbox has been modified for the installation of the hydraulic actuators designed to control the clutch travel and the gear engagement/selection movements.

INTRODUCTION

The system has the following main specifications:

- Improves the performance of the manual mechanical transmission components.

- Saves the driver having to control the clutch pedal and the conventional gear lever.

- Improves safe driving by means of a control that prevents driver errors and the incorrect operation of the transmission system.

- Offers the driver a more advanced vehicle interface.

- It is a hydraulic power assistance system for the gearbox and the clutch that maintains all the advantages of a dry clutch and a manual gearbox (weight, strength and reliability, low energy consumption).

- It is simple to use and makes driving less tiring, especially town driving.

- It ensures comfortable or sports gear changes thanks to the advanced power assistance logics.

- There is no clutch pedal in the passenger compartment and the gear lever has been replaced with "Up/Down/Neutral/Reverse" controls on a joystick on the centre tunnel.

- Automatic management of the gearbox can be enabled (by the driver) in /DRIVE mode with two different logics (NORMAL/SPORT).

There are two system operating modes for the robotized gearbox:

- SEMIAUTOMATIC Mode (MANUAL): the driver engages the gears using the lever on the tunnel.

- AUTOMATIC Mode (DRIVE): the decision to change gear depending on the engine load is delegated to the electronic system.

In addition:

- whatever mode the gearbox is in, it is possible to use a higher performance logic known as SPORT which can be activated using a dedicated button near the gear lever.

When the button is activated the gearbox uses different maps for more aggressive gear changes and the engine also responds in a different way from the NORMAL strategy. (The pedal map does not vary, but the throttle is advanced).

- there are two rocker levers on the steering wheel spokes through which it is possible to increase/decrease the gear irrespective of the speed if the gear lever is in the TIP position (between + and -). Each time it is activated by pressing the START button the system always selects the operating mode memorized the last time it was switched off.

The power assisted system consists of an electrohydraulic unit (2) fitted directly on the gearbox casing which manages the following gearbox movements by means of two actuators:

- the gear selection and engagement movement (double acting actuator)

- the control of the clutch opening.

The electrohydraulic unit is controlled by four solenoid valves (for which an electric pump and an accumulator provide the required hydraulic power).

Having identified the driver's requests from the position of the lever, an electronic control unit (1) manages the gear change independently, controlling the clutch, gearbox and engine torque directly.

The synergy between the gearbox and the engine improves the performance of the system considerably and frees the driver from any need to synchronize clutch-accelerator movements during gear changes which can be carried out with the accelerator fully depressed.

The system inhibits requests for incorrect gear changes and prevents the engine from cutting out or going outside of revs.

In terms of driving assistance the system also ensures the immediate availability of first gear when the vehicle stops and the automatic changing up through the gears in the case of strong deceleration.

The indication of the gear engaged is shown on a display in the instrument panel, in the same way as the signalling of faults or critical driving conditions for the vehicle or the transmission components with a series of warning or failure messages for the system together with the general failure or transmission failure warning lights.

ELECTROHYDRAULIC UNIT COMPONENTS

The electrohydraulic unit comes in one piece which includes three main components:

- the power unit (1) comprising the electric pump, accumulator and reservoir;

- the solenoid valve unit (2) which transforms the hydraulic energy into mechanical energy by means of the interface of the engagement pistons with the control shaft;

- the gear control mechanical unit (3) which interfaces directly with the gearbox through the opening in the actual casing;

- the clutch actuator (4) comprising the master cylinder and reservoir.

Power unit

The power unit supplies hydraulic energy for the activation of both the gear engagement/selection and the clutch master cylinder. The unit includes an electric pump (1) and a fluid reservoir (2). There is also a semi-rigid high pressure pipe (3) that connects the pressure accumulator (4) with the soleniod valve assembly and a low pressure pipe (5) that connects the valve assembly to the reservoir.

The system operates at a line pressure that varies between 36.5 and 46 bar in normal conditions. In the Recovery condition, the system can work at a pressure of 75 bar.

The electric pump is activated when the pressure goes below 36.5 bar and is deactivated when the circuit pressure reaches 46 bar.

Solenoid unit

The solenoid valve unit has the following functions:

- it controls and manages the position of the clutch

- it controls and manages the gear selection and engagement.

The components used for activating these functions are shown in the diagram.

1. Flow rate proportional solenoid valve for controlling the clutch (EV0)

2. Pressure proportional solenoid valve for even gear engagement (R - 2 - 4 - 6) (EV2)

3. Pressure proportional solenoid valve for odd gear engagement (1 - 3 - 5) (EV1)

4. On-Off solenoid valve for range selection (EV3)

5. Linear pressure sensor (0-70 bar)

6. Hall effect sensor for engagement position

7. Hall effect sensor for selection position

8. Earth points for the Selespeed control unit

Mechanical unit

The mechanical unit consists of a gear selector for choosing the suitable gear and then managing both the gear engagement and selection.

Composition

1. Control shaft

2. Gear control finger

3. "S" cam

4. Latch

5. Selection centering ball

The selector consists of a control shaft (1) which includes a double selection finger (2). The latter is capable of managing both the gear selection in the same range and that in other ranges.

The latch device (4) is capable of rotary movement to alter the selection from a lower range to a higher one and viceversa. The drum with the double "S" slot (3) makes it possible to create a rotation, through the thrust of the fluid, following a movement of the selection finger. This forces the finger to change the selection range.

This operating principle is based on the conversion of the hydraulic piston linear motion into the translation-rotatry movement of the shaft and consequently the components connected to it.

Operation

The translation movement of the shaft (which corresponds to the gear change in the same range) is implemented by two simple shifts:

- with the activation of solenoid valve EV1 or EV2, the hydraulic piston moves in a linear fashion in one direction only

- with solenoid valve EV1 the odd gears (1 - 3 - 5) are engaged and with solenoid valve EV2 the even gears are engaged (R - 2 - 4 - 6).

The movement which allows the change of the "gear branch" is activated with three shifts:

- the hydraulic brake is activated (solenoid valve EV3 is pressurized and the drum is locked)

- when one of the two chambers produced by the piston in the hydraulic cylinder is pressurized and moves in a linear fashion, the latch is forced to follow the "S" profile of the drum; in this way the shaft and therefore the selection finger is forced to follow a "translation - rotary - translation" movement which allows a change of both gear engagement and gear branch selection.

- the correct position for the branch is maintained thanks to the centering ball which acts on a surface with four channels which correspond to the four gear branches.

Electronic control unit

The control unit is located directly on the solenoid valve assembly and is connected, by means of two connections, to the engine wiring and to the gearbox hydraulic system wiring.

If the control unit is removed-refitted, in order not to damage the contact plates between the actual control unit and the solenoid valves it is advisable to use the special tool mentioned in the specific procedure.

Input signals

The system uses the following signals arriving from other vehicle systems for the operating logics:

- specific sensors from the robotized gearbox

- clutch rpm sensor (the reading is taken from the main gearbox shaft)

- position sensor for: clutch, engagement and selection

- individual signals coming from other vehicle systems

- engine rpm (signal coming from the engine management control unit via the C-CAN)

- brake pedal switch (two signals: one discreet - pin 9 vehicle connector, the other via the C-CAN)

- driver's door open switch (discreet)

- key-on (stable position and starting discreet).

The following other signals arrive from other systems via the CAN:

- accelerator pedal position

- engine torque, vehicle speed, engine temperature, etc.

Output signals

The reversing lights activation signal is no longer managed by a switch but is activated directly by the Selespeed control unit at pin 4 of the vehicle connector.

User interface

The user interfaces with the system via the following controls:

- accelerator pedal via the CAN from the engine management node

- brake pedal, via two signals: one discreet, the other via the C-CAN

- mode selection request via the multi-stable lever

- gear change request via the specific lever or via the two levers located behind the steering wheel

- SPORT mode (the signal is given by a switch connected directly to the Selespeed control unit).

The system supports the driver in the following way via the multifunction display:

- display of gear engaged (via CAN)

- "DRIVE" mode selection (via CAN)

- mode in use: "SPORT" (through the display of the letter "S")

- system failures (through a dedicated warning light coming on via the CAN)

- acoustic signal from the instrument panel buzzer: connected via the CAN, it warns the driver of a critical vehicle/system situation.

The display shows the current gear during operation in DRIVE mode.

OPERATING LOGICS

Operation of the system

Hydraulic circuit pressurization

If the pressure is below the minimum operating level, the pressurization of the hydraulic circuit takes place in two different ways:

- if the driver's door is opened the system automatically pressurizes the hydraulic circuit to allow a gear change, if requested, without waiting for the circuit to be charged (fixed pump activation time;

- with the ignition key in the OFF position: the control unit receives a power supply (and will continue to do so until the ignition key is turned OFF and the engine speed and vehicle speed are zero).

The system electric pump also receives a power supply to pressurize the system when the pressure reaches the minimum value of around 36.5 bar.

Ignition/vehicle starting

This should take place by pressing START + brake + lever in N: the engine is started by controlling the starter relay directly by the NBS control unit (steering lock node): the NBS requests a go ahead from the NCR (robotized gearbox node); the NCR responds to the NBS; the NBS allows starting.

There are emergency starting provisions if the battery is not capable of starting the engine, but the system is correctly pressurized, the vehicle can be pushed (with the clutch open) and when a sufficient speed is reached, a gear must be engaged using the selector lever; the system engages the gear that is suitable for the speed of the vehicle in order to start the engine (it is up to the driver to engage the gear and decide when the vehicle speed is fast enough to start the engine).

Operation with the engine switched off

For safety reasons, any gear change request from the lever (including neutral) is only accepted if the driver keeps the brake pedal pressed.

All the available gears can be engaged with the engine off and the electrical services activated.

Vehicle take off

The following gears can be engaged, with the engine started and the vehicle stationary, for take off:

- 1st, 2nd and Reverse; these ratios in these conditions can only be requested through moving the lever and the levers on the steering wheel.

It is vital to keep the brake pedal pressed for safety reasons when requesting engagement.

To engage Reverse, in addition to the conditions mentioned above, the vehicle must also be stationary (gearbox input revs equal to 0).

Vehicle take off is only possible if the driver operates the accelerator pedal (releasing the brake pedal); at this point, the system gradually engages the clutch to start the vehicle. The driver is capable of metering the torque transmitted from the clutch by modulating the position of the accelerator pedal; when the accelerator is released, the clutch should gradually release when a minimum engine rpm level is reached. When the system detects synchronism between the engine and clutch speeds, it closes the clutch completely. There is a specific clutch engagement map for each of the three gears enabled during take off. During take off the driver can only request a gear change when the clutch revs are the same as the engine revs (in other words at the end of the take off stage); the system is capable of managing the request during this manoeuvre.

- SPRINT departure: with the ASR off, by fully depressing the accelerator pedal, a more lively departure is achieved.

- Uphill departure: when having to overcome a steep gradient, releasing the brake pedal and activating the accelerator pedal in the end of travel position within 150 msecs produces a departure with greater engine torque. The same thing takes place by carrying out the manoeuvre with the handbrake. This strategy can also be activated on a level surface.

Automatic engagment of the clutch downhill with the accelerator pedal released

If the vehicle, with a gear engaged, the accelerator released and the engine, started picks up speed because it is going downhill, when a pre-set speed is reached, it automatically closes the clutch irrespective of the direction of travel of the vehicle to provide the vehicle with engine braking.

If the driver presses the accelerator pedal during this stage, the control of the torque transmitted by the clutch returns to the direct control of the driver.

If the engine rev conditions are too low, the clutch opens.

Vehicle slowing down

In slowing down conditions, for example with a gear engaged and the accelerator pedal released, the system automatically releases the clutch to prevent the engine from cutting out when it gets close to the idle speed.

This release takes place at an engine speed that depends on the level of deceleration and the commands implemented by the driver (brake pressed or not). Whilst slowing down, if the gear engaged is higher than 2nd, a downshift is controlled automatically (UNDERSPEED condition).

When the vehicle stops, 1st gear is engaged automatically.

Gear change using lever or levers on the steering wheel (semiautomatic operating mode)

With the vehicle moving and the clutch fully engaged, Up or Down requests from the driver via the gear lever result in a gear change.

The requests are only accepted by the system if they are compatible with the engine below revs and outside of revs limits.

As a rule, the command at the lever gives rise to an increase or decrease of one gear only, however, in certain operating conditions the gear increase may be higher than one if requested by the driver with a double fast command.

The gear change manoeuvre carried out by the driver without releasing the accelerator pedal for an up or down request, once accepted by the system, is carried out with an automatic sequence of stages that comply with the driver's behaviour:

- engine torque reduction through a command sent by the system to the engine management control unit and simultaneous clutch release.

- release, selection and engagement of the new gear, simultaneous to the gear change, managing the engine control to try and reach the speed of the clutch after the engagement of the new gear.

- modulated engagement of the clutch and simultaneous gradual return to the max torque that can be supplied by the engine at the new speed, when the system detects synchronism between the engine and clutch speeds, controlling the total engagement of the latter.

The management of the three previous phases takes place depending on:

- estimated performance requested by the driver

- estimate of the transmission temperature.

A gear change in progress can be interrupted at any time by another request from the driver as long as it is acceptable (i.e. compatible with the engine below and beyond rev limits).

The actuator control sequences during the gear change are provided with a timeout; in other words, if the gear change is not successful, it is repeated once starting from neutral, after which a higher gear than the one requested is engaged.

Automatic gear change (drive mode)

The robotized gearbox is equipped with an automatic operating mode, very similar to the one on traditional automatic transmissions.

The selection of the ratio to be engaged is made on a (double) mpa which correlates the position of the accelerator pedal and the vehicle speed.

The double map is connected to the fact that in DRIVE and MANUAL mode it is possible (using a button on the tunnel) to select the dual management of the modes defined preliminarily as SPORT and NORMAL which favours more responsive driving.

If the accelerator pedal is released, the system does not lengthen the gear, in certain conditions, in order to maintain engine braking.

The gear change mode is identical to that of the semiautomatic operation and uses the same control parameters for the gearbox and engine actuators.

Automatic engagement takes place through the lever only, placing it in an unstable manner in a specific position results in disengagement by replicating the engagement manoeuvre.

If the lever is faulty, the system works in DRIVE mode.

Request to place gearbox in neutral

This request takes priority over all other requests and can only be carried out using the lever.

The brake pedal must be kept pressed with the engine switched off as described previously.

This request for neutral is always accepted with the vehicle moving.

Switching off the engine and system

When the START button is pressed with the vehicle moving, the engine switches off and the system keeps any gear engaged.

The system is only deactivated after it sees three speeds at zero: engine, gearbox input and vehicle speed and after it has saved the operating and diagnostic data in the control unit stable memory (EEPROM).

It switches off after a maximum of around 5 seconds with the vehicle stationary and the engine switched off.

If the ignition key is turned to the OFF position when the gearbox is in neutral, the system warns the driver through a buzzer.

INFORMATION FOR THE DRIVER (DISPLAY AND BUZZER)

The system notifies the driver by means of:

- display: MANUAL operation and gear engaged, DRIVE operation, SPORT mode and the gear engaged, system failure

- buzzer: inappropriate use of the vehicle, vehicle unsafe, system failure.

Some examples of inappropriate use are listed below:

- take off with the clutch overheated.

if the system is switched off with the vehicle in neutral, the buzzer should signal the danger of leaving the vehicle switched off without the gear engaged.

Autocalibration

The following autocalibrations allow the initialization of the system in order to work properly:

- clutch bleeding

- accumulator depressurizing

- clutch autocalibration enablement

- end of line autocalibration

- end of line/service autocalibration

- new actuators

- calculation of clutch deterioration index

- deletion of statistics

- rewriting the control unit.

Clutch bleeding

This procedure is carried out using the Examiner SMART/Plus following these guidelines.

Cases in which it should be carried out:

- in the case of refilling after complete draining for hydraulic kit repair;

- after hydraulic kit repair following component replacement (valves, pump, pressure sensor, supply pipe, etc.).

- hydraulic kit general intervention.

Reasons for which it should be carried out:

- the routine is designed to eliminate the possible presence of air in the hydraulic circuit following the replacement of one of the above mentioned components carrying out 15 clutch opening/closing cycles with the oil pump activated.

Accumulator depressurization

This procedure is carried out using the Examiner SMART/Plus following these guidelines:

- before hydraulic kit repairs for component replacement (valves, pressure sensor, supply pipe, etc.).

The procedure is carried out:

- To drain the hydraulic circuit sending the fluid to the reservoir carrying out 15 clutch opening/closing cycles with the fluid pump deactivated. This results in the pressure inside the hydraulic unit decreasing.

- To check the fluid level.

Clutch autocalibration enablement

This procedure is carried out using the Examiner SMART/Plus following these guidelines:

- at the end of the line

- after replacing the Selespeed control unit

- after replacing/removing the gearbox

- after replacing/removing the hydraulic kit

- after replacing the clutch.

The procedure is carried out to quickly calculate the "kiss point" which is the position at which the clutch starts to transmit drive torque.

End of line/service autocalibration

This procedure is carried out using the Examiner SMART/Plus following these guidelines:

- at the End of the Line (where necessary)

- after replacing the gearbox

- after replacing/uncoupling the hydraulic kit

- after replacing the selection or engagement potentiometer

- after replacing the Selespeed control unit.

The procedure is carried out to memorize the thresholds for the gear change grid.

The procedure involves the automatic activation of the following functions:

- clutch closed position fast autocalibration

- clutch travel test

- clutch bleeding

- clutch Ev current autocalibration

- grid autocalibration.

New actuators

This procedure is carried out using the Examiner SMART/Plus following these guidelines:

- after replacing the hydraulic kit

- after replacing the clutch, gear selection and/or engagement solenoid valve.

The procedure is carried out to force the working losses of the solenoid valves to correspond with the values of new solenoid valves.

Calculation of the clutch deterioration index

The procedure is carried out using the Examiner SMART/Plus to allow the Selespeed control unit to calculate the clutch deterioration index due to the contribution of the engine management control unit capable of saturating the desired accelerator pedal percentage via SW and supplying the corresponding drive torque.

This procedure is necessary for the Selespeed control unit because it memorizes the typical values for each specific clutch in the Eeprom taking into account normal clutch usage over a period of time.

Deletion of statistics

This procedure is carried out using the Examiner SMART/Plus following these guidelines:

- clutch assembly replacement

- hydraulic kit replacement

- gearbox replacement

- lever replacement

- pump replacement

- accumulator replacement

- pump relay replacement

- SPORT switch replacement

- replacement of levers on the steering wheel

- statistics reset.

This procedure is carried out to zero or reset the default values for the components replaced and thereby make it possible to identify the number of incorrect conditions and manoeuvres that the system finds itself in at the time an error is validated.

Rewriting the control unit

The procedure is only carried out following the replacement of the Selespeed control unit.

This procedure is carried out to allow the system (gearbox and hydraulic kit) history to be preserved, transferring the data from one Selespeed control unit to another.

If the Selespeed control unit or any other component subject to a data deletion procedure are replaced simultaneously, the statistical data must be transcribed first and then the data relating to the component to be replaced must be deleted afterwards.

FUNCTIONAL INTERACTION WITH OTHER SYSTEMS

Interaction with engine management

Whilst driving, the two systems do not interact because the system does not carry out any work therefore there is only an exchange of information and signals via the network.

When a gear change is in progress, the system must be master over the engine management, i.e. the gearbox control system must ask the engine (via the CAN) how the engine torque should be (decreasing whilst the clutch is opening and increasing when the gear change has been completed and the clutch is closing).

Interaction with cruise control

The Cruise Control is a system that is not affected by the presence of the Selespeed system, but can only be deactivated in MANUAL mode, whilst not in DRIVE.

Abs interaction

There is no system functional interaction logic.

Asr-vdc-msr interaction

When the ASR is activated, the system should inhibit SPRINT departure.

During the operation of the ASR or VDC, the system inhibits the AUTO UP SHIFT manoeuvre.

SAFETY FUNCTIONS IN THE CASE OF FAILURE

Strategies which manage incorrect commands creating potentially dangerous or critical operating conditions for the transmission/vehicle.

Incorrect commands

- Reverse engagement: should not be accepted with the vehicle moving (above 3.5 km/h).

- Gear change with vehicle moving and clutch closed: the driver request should not be accepted if it could cause a below or above engine revs situation.

- Gear change with vehicle stationary and engine started: only gears "enabled for take off" (1st, 2nd and Reverse) should be accepted.

- Switching off using the key with the vehicle moving: the system should manage the gearbox until all the speeds monitored are zero (engine, gearbox input, gearbox output).

- Engine starting: it should be disabled if the a gear is engaged in the gearbox and the brake pedal is not pressed.

- Engine starting with gear engaged: this should only be possible with the vehicle stationary, with the accelerator pedal released, the brake pedal pressed and no faults present.

- The system should first of all place the gearbox in neutral automatically and then enable engine starting.

- With the vehicle stationary (or almost stationary), gear change requests are only accepted if the brake pedal is pressed.

- This prevents dangerous situations in the case of commands on the lever from passengers in the vehicle or persons outside the actual vehicle (e.g.: through the window !) or an undesired command by the lever on the gear control lever when the vehicle is parked on a gradient.

- Inhibition of neutral command beyond a preset speed if the accelerator pedal is pressed.

- This eliminates the risk of incorrect driver commands in critical situations (e.g.: downnhill) or inappropriate commands from passengers.

Automatic placement of the gearbox in neutral and acoustic warning for the driver (buzzer activated) when:

- the oil pressure is too low to manage the clutch.

- with the engine started, if the driver opens their door to leave the vehicle (take off with the door open is, however, allowed because the action of the driver on the brake or the accelerator is detected): placement in neutral 1.5 secs after the opening of the door.

- with the engine started, gear engaged and vehicle stationary, no accelerator or brake commands are detected for at least 3 minutes with the engine started, gear engaged and accelerator released and brake pedal pressed for at least 10 minutes.

In the presence of faults that reduce the system safety level, full operation of the vehicle is limited (e.g.: restriction to 1st, 2nd, Reverse gears when there is a fault in the gear engaged detection sensors or with the revs).

Visual/acoustic information for the driver

This information should involve:

- the operating state of the drive/vehicle system (gear display, fault warning light, buzzer).

- Acoustic signalling via the buzzer and continuous visual display through the fault warning light (associated with the specific message: "check the gearbbox"), if a fault is detected in the system I/O which therefore reduces the safety level.

- Driver information through display of gear engaged in the gearbox.

- Signalling of whether the driver has switched off the engine (key in OFF position) with the "gearbox in neutral" and therefore the vehicle could move by itself: acoustic and visual warning ("N" flashing in the display) for 4 seconds.

- Acoustic and visual signalling (display) if the system has intervened automatically placing the gearbox in neutral.

- Signalling of clutch overheating (this should be limited to when take off manoeuvres are being carried out): specific warning in the reprogrammable multifunction display and buzzer.

- Acoustic and visual signalling (display) if, after a "failed" engine starting manoeuvre, the gearbox is now in neutral.

MULTISTABLE LEVER

Description

The gear selector lever fitted on the robotized gearbox is the multistable type, i.e. with three stable positions and three unstable positions.

With reference to the diagram below, the three stable positions are those corresponding to NEUTRAL (N = NEUTRAL) REVERSE (R = REVERSE) and the TIP position [between the unstable UP (+) and DOWN (-) positions].

The unstable positions, positions that are abandoned by the lever as soon as it is released, are, as stated earlier, the higher ratio request position [UP (+)], lower gear request position [DOWN (-)] and the automatic mode reqeust position (A/M); the return to manual mode takes place by returning the lever to the A/M position.

System behaviour with vehicle stationary and engine switched off

Door opening

With the vehicle stationary, when one of the doors is opened the instrument panel is activated and various information relating to the vehicle is displayed: the gear engaged is not, however, displayed.

The pump is activated to pressurize the circuit and allow the system to be activated when there is a starting request.

Misuse before key on

At the key-off (vehicle stationary with ignition-operated electrical services deactivated):

- if the lever is in N, it is not possible to move the gear lever neither with the brake pedal released nor with the brake pedal pressed.

- if the lever is in R/TIP it is possible to move the gear lever into position N, after which the lever is mechanicall locked in N (see previous case).

The system will not carry out any activation following the movement of the lever (nor by pressing the SPORT button), therefore the gear engaged before the request from the lever (i.e. before the key-off) remains in force. No information relating to the gearbox is displayed.

Key on (+15)

With the vehicle stationary and the key in the ON position (ignition-operated electrical services activated), the instrument panel should display the gear engaged before the key off and the operating mode (automatic = D or manual = NO DISPLAY: D remains displayed even with N or R engaged) and the logic (SPORT = S or NORMAL = NO DISPLAY): the letter S is displayed in both automatic or manual mode.

The SPORT operating logic can be switched on/off (automatically or manually) by pressing the dedicated button: when the logic is engaged, the letter S is shown on the display (in both automatic or manual mode).

Shiftlock

With the vehicle stationary, the engagement of a gear from position N is only permitted if the brake pedal is pressed.

The automatic mode remains memorized at the key off (even the SPORT function) is engaged.

Misuse after the key on

When the lever is operated "with the brake pedal pressed" all the gears can be engaged.

If the lever is operated "without pressing the brake pedal", each gear change request made is not implemented by the system.

On starting the system automatically engages N.

The instrument panel (in manual operating mode and SPORT logic, if engaged) will display the request to engage neutral [N].

After cranking, the lever is already positioned in N, therefore the lever position and display are consistent.

To start the engine it is therefore necessary to:

1. press the brake and place the lever in N (in any order)

2. start the engine (always keeping the brake pressed).

STARTING THE VEHICLE FROM STATIONARY

Once the starting procedure is over, the vehicle is running, at a speed V = 0 km/h, gearbox in neutral (N) and selector lever in N.

The user can chose to set off in a forward or reverse gear.

The instrument panel, in addition to displaying the operating mode (and the SPORT logic if engaged), displays neutral "N".

Irrespective of the mode (AUTO/MANUAL) or the operating logic (SPORT/NORMAL) selected:

from lever position N:

to engage 1st or 2nd gear or Reverse, press the brake pedal:

the system enables the coil in the shift-lock and releases the lever.

Below a certain speed (10 km/h) the control unit leaves the shift-lock coil released to allow the shift from 1st to R or from R to 1st even without pressing the brake pedal. The engagement takes place in any situation until the vehicle speed is below 5 km/h. This condition ensures that the driver should not press the brake repeatedly to release the lever especially in parking situations.

with the brake pressed, therefore:

- place the lever in TIP if setting off in 1st

- place the lever in TIP and move the lever towards "+" (still pressing the brake pedal) if you decide to set off in 2nd for departures in poor grip conditions.

The levers on the steering wheel do not work because the lever is in position N.

from the TIP position or R:

- it is possible to move the lever in N even if the brake is not pressed: N is engaged.

- it is possible to shift from 1st to R or from R to 1st without pressing the brake if the manoeuvre is made quickly (parking manoeuvre); stopping in position N causes the lever to be locked: the gearbox stops operating the shift-lock coil.

- to engage 2nd, with 1st gear engaged, push towards "+"with the brake pressed.

Starting from AUTO mode: the engagement of 2nd does not involve the return to manual mode.

- the levers on the steering wheel work (if the lever is in the TIP position): it is possible to engage 1st and 2nd gear with the brake pressed (the AUTO mode is maintained if it is engaged).

ENGINE STARTED

The vehicle starts to move (take off) using the accelerator pedal only.

Only the following gears can be engaged with the engine started: 1st, 2nd or Reverse.

When R is engaged there should NOT be any ACOUSTIC WARNING.

Coming from "N" or "R" the TIP position corresponds to 1st gear.Every TIP - request is not considered by the system because it is not a plausible request.

Gear change with vehicle moving

GEAR CHANGE IN MANUAL MODE

Every gear change request for a higher ratio takes place by moving the lever to the UP + position or using the levers on the steering wheel "+".

The requests are only accepted if the gear change is over and the engine revs are such that the engine will not stall.

If the request is accepted by the system:

when the gear change is over, the display will show the new current gear.

The system shows the gear actually engaged on the display and not the gear requested by the driver.

If the request is not accepted by the system:

the gear engaged before the request will remain on the display (there is no acoustic signal).

In a similar way, the user can proceed and request lower ratios using the lever, placing it in the DOWN "-" position or via the levers on the steering wheel "-". In this case the system will only accept the request if the engine speed, after the gear change, does not exceed the maximum rotation speed permitted for the engine.

The system also automatically selects the lower ratio if the user keeps the current ratio at the engine stall speed limit (AUTODOWN manoeuvre).

The lever is in the TIP postion during the manoeuvres described above.

There is no AUTOUP.

GEAR CHANGE IN AUTOMATIC MODE

The letter D appears at the top of the display (on the left) above the indication of the gear engaged.

To move the vehicle (fowards or backwards) in spite of being in automatic mode. The driver should request the two possible gears for take off (1st or 2nd) or Reverse with the brake pressed (obviously the system will maintain the automatic mode).

the system accepts requests in this mode from the lever or the levers on the steering wheel which keep it in automatic mode.

The Kick Down function is also available: following a brisk action on the accelerator towards the end of travel position, the system recognizes the request for maximum torque and changes down by one, two or three gears if conditions allow.

SPORT/NORMAL LOGIC

In any mode by pressing the SPORT button the display also shows the letter S. Pressing the SPORT button a second time, the logic is deactivated (the letter S is no longer shown on the display (Normal logic)).

- Moving the lever or the gear lever never involves deactivating the SPORT mode: it can only be deactivated using the button.

- If the system is operating in Automatic Sport mode, placing the lever in M/D engages the Manual Sport mode (and viceversa).

REQUEST FOR NEUTRAL OR R/1ST WITH VEHICLE MOVING

Reverse gear can only be engaged in the following conditions:- brake pedal pressed- vehicle speed close to 0 km/h (below the engagement speed of 5 km/h).

Position: threshold speed greater than speed engaged

(the threshold speed coincides with the maximum speed at which the manoeuvre is permitted).

If there is a request for N or R/1st with: the vehicle speed less than or equal to the speed engaged, irrespective of the brake status, with the accelerator released:

- manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is accepted by the system; in addition to the operating mode and the logic, the display also shows neutral N.

- manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is accepted by the system; in addition to the operating mode and the logic, the display also shows R.

The vehicle speed less than or equal to the speed engaged, irrespective of the brake status, with the accelerator pressed:

- manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display.

There is also an acoustic signal.

- manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is accepted by the system; in addition to the operating mode and the logic, the display also shows R.

It is possible to make the shift from 1st to R and viceversa without pressing the brake, if the manoeuvre is made quickly (parking manoeuvres).

Speed between the speed engaged and the threshold speed (intial threshold speed = 20 km/h), irrespective of the brake with the accelerator released:

- manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is accepted by the system; N is shown on the display.

- manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is not accepted by the system which automatically engages N; N and the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" are shown on the display.

There is also an acoustic signal.

When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted.

Speed between the speed engaged and the threshold speed (intial threshold speed = 20 km/h), irrespective of the brake with the accelerator pressed:

- manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display.

There is also an acoustic signal.

- manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is not accepted by the system which automatically engages N; N and the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" are shown on the display.

There is also an acoustic signal.

When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted.

Vehicle speed above the threshold speed, irrespective of the brake, with the accelerator released:

- manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is accepted by the system; N is shown on the display.

- manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): N is not accepted and the message is "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED".

There is also an acoustic signal.

When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted.

Vehicle speed above the threshold speed, irrespective of the brake, with the accelerator pressed:

- manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display.

There is also an acoustic signal.

- manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display.

There is also an acoustic signal.

When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted.

When the lever is placed in any position, if the manoeuver is not accepted bu the lever remains in that status, as soon as the vehicle stationary conditions (vehicle speed = 0 km/h) are verified, there will be an attempt to engage neutral (N).

If the vehicle speed is equal to or less than the lock speed: the lever will be locked in N. To release it, press the brake.If the vehicle speed is greater than the lock speed: the lever will not be locked in N.

Instructions on request for Reverse/1st with vehicle speed above threshold speed

- if within a parameter time T1 (which can be calibrated) the vehicle speed is below the value of the speed engaged, the request is accepted by the system which engages reverse gear.

- if within the time T1 mentioned above, the vehicle speed remains below the threshold speed, but above the value of the speed engaged, the request (WITHOUT THE BRAKE PEDAL PRESSED) is refused by the system which engages N and the driver receives the warning message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" and there is an acoustic signal.

- if within the time T1 mentioned above the vehicle speed is maintained above the threshold speed, the request is refused by the system and the driver is warned by the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" and the acoustic signal.

In any case, if the lever is placed in "R" at any speed, without pressing the brake, with the lever remaining in this position, as soon as the system verifies that the vehicle is stationary (speed = 0 km/h), neutral is engaged.

A return from "N" or "R", either with the system either in AUTOMATIC or MANUAL, is produced by placing the lever in the stable TIP position: THE BRAKE PEDAL DOES NOT HAVE TO BE PRESSED.

The manoueuvre restores the gearbox to the most suitable gear.

SYSTEM SAFETY FEATURES

A. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R):

Press the brake and/or accelerator pedal, then open the driver's door:

the system maintains the current gear. The instrument panel continues to display the mode, the logic and the current gear; no acoustic warning.

B. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R):

Do not press the brake pedal or the accelerator pedal, then open the driver's door:

the system engages N (neutral) after around 3 seconds (which can be calibrated between 1 to 5 seconds).

The instrument panel will continue to display the mode, the logic and N.

Since the lever may be in TIP or in R, the shift to N (neutral) controlled by the system involves an inconsistent situation between the position of the lever and the gear engaged in the gearbox, therefore the manouevre is accompanied by an acoustic inconsistency signal. the sound continues until consistency is restored.

(To reinsert 1st (with the lever in TIP) it is also possible to use the levers on the steering wheel, with the brake pressed).

The use of the buzzer is planned for all cases where N is engaged automatically.

C. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R):

Never carry out any action for more than 3 minutes (which can be calibrated) (i.e. do not press either the brake pedal or the accelerator pedal and do not move the lever (e.g. stopped at traffic lights)):

the system automatically selects N (neutral).

The instrument panel will continue to display the mode, the logic and N.

Since the lever may be in TIP or in R, the shift to N (neutral) controlled by the system involves an inconsistent situation between the position of the lever and the gear engaged in the gearbox, therefore the manouevre is accompanied by an acoustic inconsistency signal. the sound continues until consistency is restored.

D. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R):

Keeping the brake pedal pressed and not carrying out any action for more than 10 minutes (which can be calibrated):

the system automatically selects N (neutral).

The instrument panel will continue to display the mode, the logic and N.

Since the lever may be in TIP or in R, the shift to N (neutral) controlled by the system involves an inconsistent situation between the position of the lever and the gear engaged in the gearbox, therefore the manouevre is accompanied by an acoustic inconsistency signal. the sound continues until consistency is restored

E. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, gearbox in neutral (N): KEY-OFF procedure:

Switch off the engine:

N flashes in the display accompanied by an acoustic warning that the vehicle has been abandonned with the gearbox in neutral (N): it flashes and sounds for about 4 seconds.

F. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, gear change other than neutral (N): KEY-OFF procedure:

Switch off the engine:

no information relating to the gearbox is displayed.
